decisions.rationale: In the title, 'breast cancer' names a single disease concept (the phrase is the paper's subject) with no further categorization, so it is a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1: Annotate all Specific Disease mentions

decisions.rationale: 'tumor' is used here to modify the noun phrase 'cell lines' ('tumor cell lines'), so it is a disease mention functioning as a Modifier. 'tumor' is explicitly retained as a disease term.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3: disease mentions used as Modifiers; What NOT to annotate 4: 'cancer' and 'tumor' retained

decisions.rationale: 'breast and ovarian cancer' is a contiguous string referring to two separate diseases (breast cancer and ovarian cancer), so it is annotated as one Composite Mention.

decisions.rationale: 'breast cancer' here modifies the noun 'biopsies' ('breast cancer biopsies'), so it functions as a Modifier of another concept rather than as a standalone disease head.

decisions.rationale: 'breast cancers' is used in the plural to refer to a family of multiple diseases, explicitly split into sporadic and familial forms, so it is a Disease Class rather than one specific disease.
